actions.reason:
Two changes in secp256r1/src/field.rs, both on the field_arith path:
1. montgomery_square used to build the 512-bit square with u128 overflowing adds and carry tracking in every column. It now uses the standard schoolbook squaring: six off-diagonal products in mac chains, doubled with a shift, then the four diagonal products added with adc. The wide product is identical, so the result is unchanged.
2. FieldElement::invert no longer converts out of Montgomery form before the almost Montgomery inverse. invert_canonical now takes a*2^256 directly and gets a^-1*2^256 = almost*2^(512-k) from the same final multiplications, which saves one Montgomery reduction per inversion. The main loop now checks for 1 only on the value it just updated (u starts at p, so it cannot be 1 at the start), instead of testing both u and v on every iteration.
The inverse is unique, so outputs are byte-identical. The equivalence harness reported identical outputs. field_arith_ir ratio 0.9653, scalar_arith_ir unchanged.

journal.text:
I rewrote montgomery_square in secp256r1/src/field.rs. The old version built the 512-bit square with u128 overflowing adds and tracked carries in every column. The new one is schoolbook squaring: six off-diagonal products in mac chains, a shift to double them, then four diagonal products added with adc. I also edited lines 277-312 and line 81 of the same file.

The first evaluation was rejected. field_arith_ir went from 374713833 to 373446221, ratio 0.9966, and the required ratio was 0.9900. The third evaluation was accepted at 361716489, ratio 0.9653, with 135 changed lines. scalar_arith_ir held at 846026188 in both runs. Outputs were identical both times. It is submitted and queued for replay.

The squaring rewrite alone barely moved field_arith_ir. Most of the gain came from the later edits around lines 277-312.

Next I want to isolate which of those edits carries the 0.9653. After that I will check whether montgomery_mul has the same per-column carry pattern.
